# Commol Documentation

> A high-performance compartment modelling library for mathematical modeling

Commol is a Python library, with a Rust engine, to build, simulate and calibrate compartment models. Models are built with ModelBuilder, simulated with Simulation and fitted with Calibrator. Examples use abstract names (bins A, B, C; parameters k1, k2).


## Getting started

- [Home](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/index.md): Overview and where to go
- [Installation](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/getting-started/installation/index.md)
- [Quick Start](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/getting-started/quickstart/index.md)

## User guide

- [Core Concepts](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/core-concepts/index.md): Compartments, stratifications, transitions, rates and initial conditions, with runnable examples
- [Model Builder](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/building-models/index.md): Every ModelBuilder method and argument, series parameters, validation rules, save and load
- [Transitions](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/transitions/index.md): Absolute and proportional rates, several sources, $compartment, category transitions, per_compartment, stratified rates, what build checks
- [Mathematical Expressions](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/mathematical-expressions/index.md): Operators, variables, subgroup totals, functions and security limits of rate formulas
- [Axis Patterns](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/axis-patterns/index.md): AxisPattern pulses, windows, ramps, sinusoids, combinations and schedules per subgroup
- [Units and Equations](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/units-and-equations/index.md): Unit checking and print_equations (text and LaTeX)
- [Running Simulations](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/simulations/index.md): Simulation.run, output formats, totals by bin and category, windowed totals, plotting
- [Calibration Basics](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/calibration/index.md): CalibrationProblem, observations, unknowns, losses, results and writing results back
- [Initial Conditions](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/calibration-initial-conditions/index.md): Calibrating bins, categories and compartments, the remainder and the order of application
- [Observations](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/calibration-observations/index.md): Several outputs, sums of outputs, weights, scale factors and windowed observations
- [Optimizers](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/calibration-optimizers/index.md): Nelder-Mead and particle swarm settings, reproducibility, troubleshooting
- [Constraints](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/calibration-constraints/index.md): Constraints on unknowns and outputs, and how violations count
- [Probabilistic Calibration](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/probabilistic-calibration/index.md): Ensembles, every configuration field, reading results, member statistics
- [Reports](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/reports/index.md): applied_parameters_report and simulation_report
- [Examples](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/examples/index.md): Complete models
